title: Eat Pizzas!
summary: Given an integer array representing pizza weights, eat exactly 4 pizzas per day to gain the weight of 1 pizza.
statement: Given an integer array representing pizza weights, eat exactly 4 pizzas per day to gain the weight of 1 pizza. On odd days, gain weight from the heaviest pizza; on even days, from the third-heaviest. Find the maximum total weight gain by optimally eating all pizzas, with n being a multiple of 4 and each pizza eaten once.
constraints: pizzas contains a positive multiple of four positive weights and every pizza is eaten exactly once.
Each day uses four pizzas; odd days gain the heaviest selected weight and even days gain the second-heaviest.
Choose daily groups to maximize total gained weight.
reference_solution:
def maximum_pizza_weight_gain(pizzas):
    pizzas=sorted(pizzas);days=len(pizzas)//4;odd=(days+1)//2;even=days-odd;answer=sum(pizzas[-odd:]);index=len(pizzas)-odd-2
    for _ in range(even):answer+=pizzas[index];index-=2
    return answer

hints: Largest weights should be reserved for odd-day maxima; each even-day gain needs one larger sacrificial pizza.
Sort, take the largest odd-day count directly, then take every second remaining value for even days.
Let odd=ceil(days/2); sum that many largest weights, skip one larger partner before each even gain, and use smallest leftovers as fillers.
Exchange arguments move any larger gain candidate into an odd slot or the best feasible even second position without decreasing the total.
editorial: Exchange arguments move any larger gain candidate into an odd slot or the best feasible even second position without decreasing the total.

tests.explanation: Use eight as the odd-day maximum and place seven above six on the even day, gaining eight plus six equals fourteen.
The sole odd day gains the heaviest pizza, four.
